decoded.meaning: The FORWARDED leg of a mint-flagged READ: FWD{ op=0x80 = READ | mint-request, dst=/temp (the residual after this hop consumed /sensor), src=/net/a (grown canonically by the arrival mount), PATH_REF_REVERSE(1 element) }. The trailing 0x15 child is the reverse-direction list the forwarding hop contributed — its own reference to the identity the request arrived on (RFC-0024 §7.1 amendments 1 and 2). The origin's own frame carries no such child: fwd/fwd-mint-request is what the origin emitted, unchanged.
decoded.note: The reverse list is identified by its TYPE — 0x15 PATH_REF_REVERSE — and never by its position (RFC-0024 §7.1 amendment 2). Its body grammar is 0x14's exactly: opt.PL and opt.LL both 0, length a multiple of 8, at most 255 elements. A reader that identified it as 'the only trailing child' would mis-read a mint-flagged WRITE whose payload is a raw PATH_REF, which is the shape the amendment gives back.
